response.report:
EXAM: Chest radiograph, one view, 2026-11-12
CLINICAL INDICATION: Routine surveillance. History of treated breast cancer. No new symptoms.
ORDERING PROVIDER: Dr. L. Okafor (synthetic), medical oncology
COMPARISON: Chest radiograph, 2026-02-10
TECHNIQUE: Current PA, prior PA. No contrast. Differences from prior: current inspiration is slightly deeper (right dome projects a little lower); current has slightly greater penetration and contrast, so lung markings and vertebrae behind the heart are more conspicuous; shoulder, arm and breast position differ (left breast shadow overlaps more of the left base on the prior, and the left chest device projects higher on the current). Both studies are adequate and comparable. Both images are downsampled, which limits fine detail.

LOOK AT FIRST:
- None time-sensitive. Priority review order: (1) F2, indeterminate right lower zone small dense focus and markings; (2) F1, device finding, reads disagreed. Triage: urgency high, on-call page not indicated. Reason: possible new small right lower zone nodule after breast cancer, reads uncertain, needs radiologist review of source images.

FINDINGS (systematic read, done blind to the indication):
- Airway / lungs: Trachea central, no narrowing. Lungs well expanded. No consolidation, mass or collapse. Linear bronchovascular markings are mildly prominent in the medial right lower zone, with a single small dense nodular focus projected among them (F2, indeterminate; both reads indeterminate). The markings are more conspicuous than on the prior, but the current film is more penetrated with higher contrast, which might explain this. The nodular focus is not clearly seen on the prior. Left lung clear. Apices clear.
- Mediastinum / hila: Prominent rounded aortic knuckle, consistent with an unfolded aorta (F3, similar to prior). Upper mediastinum not widened. Hila normal in position, no one-sided hilar enlargement.
- Pleura: No pleural line to suggest pneumothorax. Both costophrenic angles sharp. No pleural thickening. Both domes well defined. No free gas under the diaphragm.
- Heart: Cardiac silhouette not enlarged on PA view, borders distinct, similar to prior (F4; only one of the two reads recorded this finding). Heart width is slightly smaller on the current, in keeping with deeper inspiration.
- Bones / soft tissue: No rib, clavicle or shoulder fracture or destructive lesion seen at this resolution. Visible spine aligned. Bilateral breast shadows overlie the lower zones. No soft tissue gas. Device (F1): INDETERMINATE, the two blind reads disagreed (read A: stable; read B: indeterminate). Thin tubing arcs across the left upper zone from the medial left clavicular region to a small metallic component over the lateral left upper to mid zone, described as consistent with an implanted venous access port and catheter. The same configuration is present on both studies and projects higher on the current, in keeping with different arm and breast position. No kink or discontinuity seen at this resolution. Catheter tip not traced over the mediastinum. Note for reviewer: the F1 finding description reads external monitoring leads on one film with no implanted device identified, which conflicts with the systematic read and the cant-determine items. Please verify on source images.

INTERVAL CHANGE:
- Changed: No confirmed change. F2 (right lower zone markings and small dense focus) appears more conspicuous on the current, but this is indeterminate and may be due to exposure and contrast differences. The left chest device projects higher on the current, possibly positional; true migration is not established.
- Unchanged: Aortic knuckle prominence and mediastinal contour (similar). Cardiac silhouette not enlarged (similar). No pneumothorax, pleural thickening or free subdiaphragmatic gas on either study. Left lung clear.

RECIST 1.1: Not computed on radiographs. No confirmed measurements. A measurement entry for F2 (prior 12 mm, current 13 mm) was supplied but is not used: the findings state no pixel scale is available, and the focus is not clearly seen on the prior. Size change for F2 is not stated.

CAN'T DETERMINE:
- Is the small dense focus in the medial right lower zone a true lung nodule, and is it new? | Reason: The focus is small and lies among vessels, so a vessel seen end-on or a calcified granuloma cannot be separated from a nodule on a frontal film. The softer exposure of the prior may hide it. | Recommend: Review the source images in PACS. If it persists, CT chest. (read A)
- Have the right lower zone lung markings truly increased since the prior? | Reason: The current study is more penetrated with higher contrast, which makes fine markings more conspicuous without a real change. | Recommend: Review source images side by side in PACS with matched windowing. Interval follow-up PA film, or CT chest if there is clinical concern. (read A; related to F2)
- Where is the tip of the left-sided venous catheter? | Reason: The thin catheter cannot be followed over the dense mediastinal shadow on these low-resolution frontal images. | Recommend: Review the source image in PACS with edge-enhanced windowing, or obtain a lateral view. (read A; related to F1)
- Where is the tip of the left-sided venous catheter, and has it moved? | Reason: The catheter is lost over the dense mediastinal shadow on both films at this resolution. The chest wall component projects at a different rib level on the two films. | Recommend: Review the source images in PACS with window adjustment. Add a lateral view if tip position matters clinically. (read B; related to F1)
- Is the tiny dense focus over the right lower zone on current a nodule, a vessel end-on or a calcified granuloma, and is it new? | Reason: The focus is too small for a frontal X-ray to separate a nodule from a vessel end-on or a bone island. On prior the same area is covered by breast shadow on a lower contrast film. | Recommend: Review the source image in PACS. CT chest if it persists or is of clinical concern. (read B)
- Are the more conspicuous right lower zone markings on current a real interval change? | Reason: Breast shadow overlap, contrast and depth of inspiration differ between the two films. | Recommend: Correlate clinically. Repeat PA and lateral with matched technique, or CT chest if concern persists. (read B; related to F2)
- Are the faint linear densities lateral to the left hilum on prior a real band of atelectasis or scarring, and have they cleared? | Reason: Mild rotation and lower contrast on prior. Vessels and the overlying catheter cross the same area. The appearance is not reproduced on current. | Recommend: Review the source images in PACS. No further imaging needed if the radiologist confirms normal vessels. (read B)
- Is there a subtle rib, spine or shoulder lesion? | Reason: The low resolution, compressed image limits fine bone detail. Shoulders and ribs are partly overlapped by soft tissue. | Recommend: Review the source images in PACS on bone settings. Dedicated imaging if there is focal pain or clinical concern. (read B)

IMPRESSION:
1. Indeterminate small dense nodular focus with more conspicuous linear markings in the medial right lower zone (F2). Both reads were indeterminate. The focus is not clearly seen on the prior, and the greater penetration and contrast of the current film might explain the markings. In a patient with treated breast cancer, a new nodule cannot be excluded or confirmed on this study. Needs review of source images.
2. Left chest device (F1) indeterminate; the two blind reads disagreed. Same configuration on both studies, projecting higher on the current, possibly positional. Catheter tip not determined. The F1 description conflicts with the systematic read and needs verification.
3. No mass, pleural effusion, hilar or mediastinal enlargement, or destructive bone lesion seen at this resolution, apart from the indeterminate findings above.
4. Prominent aortic knuckle (F3) and non-enlarged cardiac silhouette (F4) are similar to the prior.

RECOMMENDATIONS:
- Review source images in PACS side by side with matched windowing, including bone settings and edge-enhanced windowing for the catheter.
- CT chest if the right lower zone focus persists on source image review or there is clinical concern (interval not specified in the findings).
- If concern persists about the right lower zone markings, interval follow-up PA film or repeat PA and lateral with matched technique (interval not specified in the findings).
- Lateral view if catheter tip position matters clinically.

AI DRAFT: requires resident review and attending signature.
